content_md:
The most basic, atomic hyperstition is the belief that “I am important and special.” It can work even if you only perform the belief without holding it yourself.

It’s astounding how far you can get simply by acting as though your own importance is a self-evident truth. Humans are primed to adopt and believe in such postures by default and follow those who affect it most confidently. And that kind of following is often sufficient to make it true. And this can happen even when that posture looks obviously false to discerning observers, and a case of self-importance based on nothing. The thing is, you don’t have to convince the discerning. Only the gullible. Like Nigerian prince scams, hyperstitional self-importance only needs a small vulnerable minority to work.

Almost all the misery in the world is due to the fact that this works.
